source_text: Quid ergo vis, subtilissime disputator? Sacrilegam esse in Dei operibus verecundiam, quia omnia quae Deus fecerit, passim agi debeant, ne nostra trepidatio opificem videatur arguere? Erravit ergo apostolus Paulus, qui Dei opera describens, ait: Verecundiora nostra maiorem honestatem habent; et Deus temperavit corpus, ei cui deerat abundantiore dato honore, ut non sit scissura in corpore [n58] .
pass_a_gloss: What therefore do you want, most subtle disputant? That reverence in God's works is sacrilegious, because all things which God has made ought to be done everywhere, lest our trembling seem to accuse the craftsman? Therefore the apostle Paul erred, who describing God's works says: Our more shameful parts have greater honor; and God tempered the body, giving more abundant honor to that which was lacking, so that there may not be a schism in the body.

lemmas.lexica: LS opus; Blaise God's works vs devil's

pass_b_english: What, then, do you mean, most subtle disputant? Is modesty about God’s works sacrilegious, because everything God has made must be done openly, lest our hesitation seem to accuse the craftsman? Then the apostle Paul was wrong when he described God’s works and said, “Our less respectable parts receive greater honor; and God arranged the body, giving more abundant honor to the part that lacked it, so that there should be no division in the body” (1 Corinthians 12:23–25).

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.
